newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FedEx to start Internet sales in Singapore.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to start Internet sales in Singapore.

text.p: Freight forwarder Federal Express Corp (FedEx) said on Wednesday it would introduce Internet-based electronic commerce in Singapore middle of the year.
"With the dawning of the age of electronic commerce, it has become an exciting period for FedEx," said John Allison, vice president for South Pacific.
Speaking at a news conference, Allison said the system would get pilot trials in Singapore before being introduced for Asia.
The exact timeframe for implementation was not disclosed and Allison declined to give details of the revenue expected to be earned via Internet-based systems.
Total FedEx revenues were US$10.3 billion in fiscal 1996.
FedEx began experimenting with Internet transactions for customers from its U.S. headquarters in April last year.
An Internet service provider had been identified in Singapore and testing of systems with customers would soon begin, Allison said.

He revealed the Internet plans after announcing that FedEx had secured certification ISO9002 for its quality procedures from The International Standards Organisation at all 10 of its Asia express distribution centres.
Three more centres in Taiwan, Seoul and Beijing, due to be opened by the end of April would also be rated soon after opening.
FedEx has "ambitious plans for the millennium", said Allison, including increasing flights from Singapore around the region and adding services to China and Thailand.
Allison said FedEx would also open new express centres in the region, but the locations of these were not disclosed.
